title: McKinney's Cotton Pickers and Harlem bandleaders
summary: Campbell remembers tuba and bass players, Don Redman and Harlem big bands.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: I'm thinking about a 45 I've got at my mother's house with Hot Lips Page and Pearl Bailey doing "Baby Its Cold Outside," a duet.
Oh, yeah, okay. These are McKinney's Cotton Pickers.
Yeah, that's the band that I told you this fella named Waterhouse --(ed.-Frank)
McKinney's Cotton Pickers, what's the musician you're talking about?
Oh, My God, I can't think of it now, it'll come to me, "If I Could Be With You One Hour Tonight."
He played an E-flat tuba and string bass, like my dad did, yeah, and Don Redman played a whole lot of instruments. Don was something else, yeah. His main instrument was a

tenor sax I think, yeah. McKinney Cotton Pickers. Did you know Ed Bonnelly? John C. Smith, they were big bands in Harlem. Did you know Vernon Andrade? He played at the Renaissance Ballroom.
Yeah, I heard of him but I don't think I --
He had Claude Fats Green who used to play a baritone sax, he went with Duke later on.
